entry.title: Material BOM Migration (2602) - BOM Item Document Assignment - Error 29 356 although complete docume

However, during the Migration Simulation, the process fails with the following error:

  • Message Class: 29

The document exists in the system with the following key:

  • Document Type: ZBO
  • Document Number: 10000000003
  • Document Version: A
  • Document Part: 000
  • Status: H3 (Released)

Migration Template Details

BOM Item

  • BOM Usage = 1
  • Alternative BOM = 2
  • Item ID = 00000002
  • Item Category = D

BOM Item Document Assignment

The following fields are maintained:

  • Material Number
  • Plant
  • BOM Usage
  • Alternative BOM
  • Item ID = 00000002
  • Document Type = ZBO
  • Document Number = 10000000003
  • Document Version = A
  • Document Part = 000

Verification Already Performed

  • The Document Info Record exists in the system.
  • The document status is valid (H3 – Released).
  • Manual assignment of the same document to the BOM works successfully.
  • All document key fields are maintained in the BOM Item Document Assignment worksheet.
  • The Item ID in the BOM Item sheet matches the Item ID in the BOM Item Document Assignment sheet.

Has anyone successfully migrated BOM document assignments (Item Category D) using the Material BOM migration object in Release 2602?

entry.title: [S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition] How to enter amounts and currencies for foreign-currency cash
entry.content:
[Title]
[S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition] How to enter amounts and currencies for foreign-currency cash / receivables / payables in the Migration Cockpit (transaction, company code and group currency)

[Body]
Hello everyone,

I would appreciate your guidance on how to enter the amount and currency fields when migrating foreign-currency balances and open items in the Migration Cockpit (Migrate Your Data, staging table approach) of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (release: XXXX).

System setup
- The company has its headquarters in Japan. Company code currency = JPY, group (global) currency = JPY.
- USD is used as a transaction currency.

Migration objects in scope
- FI - G/L Account Balances and Open Items
- FI - Accounts Receivable Open Items
- FI - Accounts Payable Open Items

Scenario
I want to migrate a situation where cash, a receivable and a payable are each held as 50,000 USD.
For each sheet, I would like to confirm what exactly should go into the following three amount/currency fields:
- Transaction currency
- Company code currency
- Group currency

Questions
1. For the transaction-currency fields, is it correct to enter currency = USD and amount = 50,000?
2. For the company code currency (JPY) and group currency (JPY) amount fields, do I need to enter the JPY-converted amount myself, or should I leave them blank and let the system translate?
3. If the system translates, which exchange rate is applied (migration key date / posting date / a customized exchange rate type)? If I enter a value manually, does the manual amount take precedence over the system translation?
4. When both the company code currency and the group currency are JPY, can I enter the same value in both JPY amount fields, or is a separate entry required per currency type?
5. For open items (AR/AP), should I manually enter the JPY amount converted at the historical rate (as of the posting date) at line-item level, to stay consistent with the balances? Is there any difference in approach between the G/L balances side and the open-items side?

My current assumption
I am assuming that I enter USD 50,000 in the transaction currency and manually enter the amount converted at the posting-date rate on the JPY side (company code and group currency), but I would like to confirm the standard expected behavior, the mandatory fields, and the rate-application logic.

If you could also let me know the relevant release and the corresponding staging structure names (e.g., S_BSIS), I can verify against those field names as well. Thank you in advance.

NR for BPIN: 90000000 - 90999999 internal

Have you done something like that and do you have a hint what to do?

Thanx in advance!!!!

entry.title: [BUG] Migration Cockpit template XML is not well-formed and opens only in Excel - S/4HANA Cloud
entry.content:
Disclaimmer:
For fellow implementers: if you use the Migration Cockpit and work with
LibreOffice, WPS Office, Google Sheets or Microsoft 365 for the web (for
example on Linux), you have probably seen the downloaded templates fail to
open. This is not an installation problem on your side. Below is the cause,
how to confirm it, and a workaround.

For SAP S/4HANA developers: this is a bug report. The template generator
writes unescaped markup into the XML, so the file is not well-formed. The
exact location, a reproduction and the expected behaviour are below.
Hi all,

We download master data migration templates from the SAP S/4HANA Migration
Cockpit. The files are declared as "Microsoft Excel XML Spreadsheet 2003", but
they only open in Microsoft Excel for desktop. LibreOffice Calc, WPS Office,
Google Sheets and Microsoft 365 for the web all fail to open them.

Environment
- Template version string: SAP S/4HANA CLOUD 2602 - Adjusted Scope - 22.07.2026
- Migration object: Supplier (template title VENDOR_2)
- Template language: EN

After investigating, the file is simply not well-formed XML. The "Introduction"
sheet, cell C8, carries SAP documentation markup that was written into the cell
text without XML escaping (source lines 353-355):

<Data ss:Type="String">... In the file, navigate to <LS>File </>->
<LS>Info</>. You can find the active view name under <LS>Properties
</>-> <LS>Tags</>.</Data>

"</>" is not a valid XML end tag, and "<LS>" is never closed. Any strict parser
stops right there.

xmllint:
parser error : Opening and ending tag mismatch: LS line 353 and unparsable

LibreOffice Calc:
malformed_xml_error: name must begin with an alphabet,
but got this instead '>' (offset=16142)

LibreOffice shows no error to the user - it just opens an empty spreadsheet,
which is why this initially looked like a failed download on our side.

One detail that may help narrow it down: a different paragraph in the same
Introduction sheet writes the same kind of menu path as plain quoted text -

navigate to 'File' -> 'Options' -> 'Advanced'

- so only this one paragraph carries the markup. There are 8 occurrences in
total (4x "<LS>", 4x "</>") and all of them sit in that single cell. The rest of
the document is well-formed. The text itself is generic template boilerplate,
not Supplier-specific.
 
Your migration cockpit looks like it is neither escaping nor validating the cell text when it generates the template. Documentation markup (<LS>…</>) is copied into the XML verbatim, and the result is never checked for well-formedness before it is offered for download. Excel's lenient parser hides the problem, but any standards-compliant parser rejects the file.

What we have tried
- Re-downloading the template: same result.
- Escaping the angle brackets by hand: the file then validates and opens in
every application we tested.
- As a workaround we now pre-process each template with a small script that
escapes the stray markup and rewrites the workbook as .xlsx. OR just remove the <LS> tags and its end tags </>

My questions
1. Is this a known issue? Is there an SAP Note, or a release where it is fixed?
2. Are all migration objects affected, or does the Introduction sheet content
differ per object?
3. Is the intended behaviour that this documentation markup is rendered to plain
text ("navigate to File -> Info") before the template is generated?

Thanks in advance.
